skill_concept: Patching an existing Makefile to fix compiler identity or flags (including cross-compilation toolchain targets) and rebuilding with make
verdict_reason: Both tasks involve patching a Makefile and rebuilding, but make-doom-for-mips requires a fundamentally more complex procedure: a full LLVM-based cross-compilation pipeline with custom toolchain stages (clang -> llc -> mips-linux-gnu-as -> mips-linux-gnu-ld), custom stdlib shims, and architecture-specific flags — far beyond patching a compiler variable or a flag line. A skill written to cover both would have to be so abstract it loses actionable specificity.
weakest_link_reason: The MIPS task is not a simple Makefile patch; it requires designing a multi-stage cross-compilation toolchain from scratch, adding source files, and managing MIPS-specific ABI details, which goes well beyond the candidate skill's scope of fixing compiler identity or flags.
